findings.description: The diff output begins with '* Unmerged path .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh'. The fence hunk this sprint is supposed to add (the '# @guard fence:<id>' markers, the 'replay: true' audit field under LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1, the FR-1.2b message change) is therefore absent from the review input, and the working tree holds a conflicted copy of the single most important harness guard. Per the hook:hook-guard.sh row added in guard-origins.yaml, hook-guard.sh runs 'bash -n' on the wrapped hook and 'fails a broken one open instead of bricking the tool'. A file carrying conflict markers does not parse, so for as long as this state exists every fence row is disabled, including fence:FR-1.2b and the 15 fence:FR-SZ*/FR-SZ2* rows that floor.yaml declares as the floor. guard-yield.sh also reads this file for its marker cross-check and would scan both conflict sides.
findings.failure_mode: Destructive commands and System-Zone shell writes pass unblocked in any session that loads the conflicted hook; the fence behavioural and audit changes merge without having been reviewed, and the reviewer's concern about LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY hiding real blocks cannot be assessed.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the merge conflict, confirm 'bash -n' passes and the fence corpus still reports 78/100/5, run '.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --check', and re-submit the diff with the fence hunk included so the markers, the replay field and the FR-1.2b change can be reviewed.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.anchor: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:hooks (while IFS="$US" read -r tag ev mt rel wrapped loop)
findings.description: The containment check for a registered hook script tests only the final path component: '[[ -L "$abs" ]]' then one readlink. If an intermediate directory under .claude/ is a symlink (for example .claude/hooks/ext -> /opt/anything), a command of the canonical shape '"$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"/.claude/hooks/ext/run.sh' passes the schema regex, '-f' succeeds through the directory link, the id becomes hook:ext/run.sh and no 'leaves .claude/' error fires. The badpath check only rejects '.', '..' and empty segments, so it does not help here. The script's stated purpose is that a command can only resolve to a script inside .claude/.
findings.failure_mode: The register and hooks table attest a hook as living under .claude/ when it executes code from outside the repository; the 'symlink that leaves .claude/' guard is bypassable by a directory link.
findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalise the whole path for every hook, not just final-component symlinks: canon="$(cd "$(dirname "$abs")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$abs")" and, if the basename is itself a link, resolve it in a loop; then require canon to start with "$ROOT/.claude/". Reject when the resolved file is not a regular file.

findings.description: floor.yaml says the floor is 'the set of guards ... no profile, knob or cycle task may weaken', and pins the bytes of adversarial-review-gate.sh, verdict-derive.sh, settings.deny.json and user-invoked-commands.txt. It does not pin the hook registrations in .claude/settings.json (or settings.hooks.json), and guard-yield.sh does not require that a floor gate whose script is a hook is actually registered. A cycle task can (1) delete the safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh entry from settings.json and (2) delete the hook:safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh row from guard-origins.yaml, then regenerate. guard-yield.sh --check passes (the gate:adversarial-review-gate row remains, its script exists, floor sets agree), floor-snapshot passes (no floor_files byte changed), and the COMPLETED-marker gate never runs again. The same applies to policy:permission-deny-list, whose live rules are the permissions.deny list in settings.json rather than the pinned settings.deny.json.
findings.failure_mode: A floor gate is silently disabled by editing two non-floor files; the register continues to list it as active and floor.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add .claude/settings.json (or the hooks section source) to floor_files, or extend guard-yield.sh's cross-check: for every row with floor: true whose script lies under .claude/hooks/, require an enumerated hook row with that script and a non-empty registrations list, exit 5 otherwise. Consider also pinning the permissions.deny array by content.

findings.description: Before this change stash-safety.md loaded unconditionally. The new frontmatter scopes it to '**/*.sh', '**/*.bats', '.claude/scripts/**' and '.claude/hooks/**', so the harness only injects it when the model reads or edits a matching file. The rule's subject is the model running 'git stash push/pop' through the Bash tool, with pre-commit hooks' own --keep-index stash shifting indexes. That action is taken while editing any file type (a .ts or .md change during /implement) and needs no .sh file in context, so the rule is now absent in exactly the sessions it was written for. The FR-1.2b fence still catches the swallowed-output shape, but the plain 'git stash pop' hazard the prose describes is unfenced.
findings.failure_mode: Model issues git stash wraps in a session that never touched a shell file; the prose guard is not loaded and the stash-safety guidance is silently withdrawn.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the paths frontmatter for this rule (keep it unconditional), or widen the globs to the files touched during the workflows where stashing happens, and record the decision in the rule-paths.bats expectations.

findings.description: The yield spec in the header (and the BURST_ROWS=10 constant) classifies any UTC minute holding 10 or more block rows as a fixture replay, justified by 'no interactive session blocks ten commands in one minute'. The primary consumer of these guards is run mode, which is not interactive: a model thrashing against a blocked redirect into .claude/ or an rm -rf variant routinely retries several shapes within seconds, and the FR-SZ family fires once per attempt. Those minutes are real catches, and the heuristic reclassifies all of them as replays. The implementation of the heuristic is in the part of the file not present in the diff, so only the specified behaviour is reviewed here.
findings.failure_mode: blocks_30d and last_real_catch under-count exactly the guards that fire hardest; a guard that caught a real burst reads as idle in .run/guard-yield.md and may be retired on that evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the burst rule only to rows that predate the replay flag and lack a replay field, and additionally require a replay signature (cwd under TMPDIR or a bats/evals/sandbox path, or distinct command fixtures repeating) before discarding; count run-mode bursts separately as 'burst_30d' rather than as replays.

findings.description: render_hooks_ref validates that hooks-reference.md contains exactly one begin and one end marker by count only. If the end marker precedes the begin marker (a hand edit, or a bad merge of the generated block), the awk pass drops the end marker (skip=0, next), later hits the begin marker, prints the block, sets skip=1 and never clears it, so every line after the begin marker is discarded from the rewritten file. Also, if the block file fails to open, getline returns -1 and both markers are consumed with no table written, leaving a file that the next --check rejects with 'found 0 and 0'.
findings.failure_mode: A --hooks-table run truncates the tracked hooks-reference.md after the marker, or removes the markers entirely; recoverable from git but silently committed if not noticed.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the line numbers of the two markers with grep -n and require begin < end before rewriting; have the awk exit non-zero if the block file cannot be read, and compare the output's line count to the input's outside the block before replacing the file.

findings.description: Review coverage note for the primary reviewer. The guard-yield.sh hunk is declared as 625 lines but the diff ends after render_hooks_ref at roughly line 330, so the yield computation (window filtering, replay and false-positive heuristics, privacy of .run/guard-yield.*), the --check comparison, the --json output and the main dispatch were not available. None of the other files named in the reviewer context are in the diff: execute-agent.sh arm toggles, run-arms.sh and its worktree/env scrub, seed-corpus-from-record.sh redaction, validate_sprint_kinds in validate-artifact.sh, cycle-ratio.sh SHA handling, and the loa-status.sh LOA_STATUS_GUARDS_FILE seams. Concerns 1 (yield/--check purity/privacy), 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are therefore unverified by this pass, not cleared.
findings.failure_mode: A problem in the unreviewed half of guard-yield.sh or in the absent scripts reaches main with the dissent artefact implying it was examined.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the dissent with the complete guard-yield.sh hunk and the remaining sprint files included, or record in the review artefact that those items were out of the reviewed diff.
